A row group is a logical horizontal partitioning with no guaranteed physical structure of its own — the guarantee is only that a row group's column chunks are contiguous in the file, not that row groups themselves are any particular size.

at.step: Reveal: row group, column chunk, page

items.item: The footer is written last specifically because it lets a writer produce the file in a single forward pass without knowing in advance where every column chunk will end up — not an arbitrary format choice.

at.step: Reveal: the footer is written last

items.item: A dictionary page is optional per column chunk; a reader must check for its presence (via the optional dictionary_page_offset field) rather than assume one exists, which this topic's own second row group demonstrates by omitting it.

at.step: Reveal: dictionary page vs. data page

items.item: The entire structural difference between a v1 DATA_PAGE and a v2 DATA_PAGE_V2 header is that v2 keeps repetition and definition levels uncompressed and separate from the value section, letting a reader learn row/null counts without decompressing values — not a difference in what data each page can represent.

at.step: Reveal: the same column, v1 vs v2

items.item: INT96's 12 bytes carry no timezone information at all; any apparent agreement between two readers interpreting those bytes is coincidence, not correctness, which is why the format deprecated it in favor of a logical type with an explicit flag.

at.step: Reveal: the INT96 timestamp pitfall

items.item: isAdjustedToUTC does not change how the underlying integer is encoded (still milliseconds/microseconds/nanoseconds since an epoch) — it only removes the ambiguity about which epoch-relative meaning that integer has.

at.step: Reveal: isAdjustedToUTC closes the gap

items.item: A column's physical type (how its bytes are laid out) and its logical type (what those bytes mean) are two separate fields in the same SchemaElement — a column can have a physical type with no logical type at all, as this topic's own legacy INT96 column does.

This topic's hand-rolled file was independently verified against a real Parquet implementation (pyarrow), confirming the Thrift Compact Protocol encoding and the page/footer byte layout are genuinely spec-compliant, not merely self-consistent with this topic's own reader.
Column statistics, page-level indexes and bloom filters are deliberately out of scope here — they are the next topic's own subject (§6.2, data skipping), built on top of exactly this file anatomy.

Table formats (Iceberg, Delta Lake) add a stable, format-level column ID on top of a file format like Parquet's own schema, which this topic's file does not use — that comparison belongs to this chapter's later table-format topics, not this one.
